title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of Judicial Convenience for the People
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of Facilitating Litigation for the People"

Fa Fa [2009] No. 6

The Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

We hereby issue to you the "Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of Facilitating Litigation for the People." Please earnestly implement them in light of local conditions.

February 13, 2009

Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of Facilitating Litigation for the People

Under the new historical conditions, satisfying the people's new demands and expectations for court work through solid and effective efforts is an inevitable requirement for the people's courts to implement the guiding ideology of "the Party's cause above all else, the people's interests above all else, and the Constitution and laws above all else," to thoroughly apply the Scientific Outlook on Development, and to strive to solve specific problems in serving the people through justice. It is the fundamental starting point and ultimate goal of all work of the people's courts. To further strengthen and standardize the work of the people's courts in facilitating litigation for the people and to meet the requirements of the new situation, these opinions are hereby formulated.

1. The people's courts shall establish case filing halls or litigation service centers, equip them with necessary staff, and earnestly perform work in areas such as receiving complaint letters and visits, providing litigation guidance, case inquiry, contacting case-handling personnel, receiving and forwarding litigation materials, answering litigation questions, providing post-judgment clarification, and guiding litigants in reasonably selecting dispute resolution methods. Necessary service facilities shall also be provided.

2. The people's courts shall establish systems for case filing and receiving complaint letters and visits on non-working days as needed. The people's tribunals may directly accept cases within the scope of their authorization. The basic people's courts may accept case filings by appointment through telephone or the internet, and may provide door-to-door case filing and other convenient services for litigants who are injured, ill, disabled, elderly, or have mobility difficulties, to facilitate their litigation.

3. The people's courts shall do a good job of providing litigation risk warnings. When accepting case filings, they shall provide litigants with a litigation risk warning letter and a notification of litigation rights and obligations to help litigants understand litigation risks, rights, and obligations.

4. The basic people's courts shall establish and improve mechanisms for the diversified handling of simple and complex cases and for fast-track adjudication, focusing on resolving disputes through mediation, quickly resolving conflicts, and improving litigation efficiency.

5. The basic people's courts shall strictly implement the legal provisions on the application of summary procedures for trying cases. Upon the application of a litigant and with the consent of the opposing party, the people's court may further simplify relevant aspects of the summary procedures in accordance with the law, giving full play to the efficiency advantages of summary procedures.

For cases tried under ordinary procedures, upon the application of a litigant and with the consent of all parties, the people's court may simplify the procedures for trial in accordance with the law.

6. The basic people's courts shall actively conduct circuit trials based on local conditions. For remote areas or areas with concentrated disputes, the people's tribunals shall conduct circuit case handling regularly or irregularly, accepting cases on the spot, trying cases on the spot, mediating immediately, concluding cases immediately, and enforcing judgments on the spot. Upon the request of the litigants, the basic people's courts and people's tribunals may hold court sessions at a reasonable time mutually agreed upon by the litigants.

7. Where a litigant applies to the people's court for investigation and evidence collection and meets the conditions prescribed by law, the people's court shall promptly investigate and collect evidence. Where the conditions prescribed by law are not met, the people's court shall promptly notify the litigant and guide the litigant to investigate and collect evidence on their own in accordance with the law. For litigants who are genuinely unable to investigate and collect evidence, the people's court may investigate and collect evidence upon the litigant's request and as needed for the trial of the case.

8. The people's courts may invite deputies to the People's Congress, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), and ordinary people from the grassroots to assist in litigation work, assisting the people's courts in mediating and enforcing cases. With the consent of the litigants, the people's court may entrust the case to the people's mediation committee, relevant administrative departments, social organizations, or grassroots people's organizations to preside over mediation. If a mediation agreement is reached, it shall be confirmed by the people's court in accordance with the law.

9. Improve the system for the public to observe court trials. For cases that the people's court decides to hear in open session, it shall strictly announce the hearing information in accordance with the law to facilitate the public in observing the trial. Applicants who meet the conditions for observing the trial shall be issued a pass for observation or be allowed to observe directly upon production of their identity documents. The people's courts shall regularly invite deputies to the People's Congress and members of the CPPCC to observe court trials.

10. The people's courts shall gradually establish a system for public inquiry of adjudicatory documents and litigation archives. Where conditions permit, the people's courts may publicly disclose adjudicatory documents and information on enforcement cases online in accordance with the law.

11. In handling cases involving enforcement, retrial review, commutation and parole, and state compensation, the people's courts may implement an open hearing system to consciously accept supervision by litigants and the public over court work.

12. The people's courts shall strengthen trial management, implement a system for monitoring the time limits for adjudication, strictly enforce conditions for extending case time limits, and increase the rate of case conclusion and enforcement completion within the prescribed time limits. Do a good job of transferring case files from first instance, second instance, and retrial, clarifying the time limit for transfer, unifying the method of transfer, defining the responsibility for transfer, and solving the problem of difficulty in transferring case files.

13. The language of adjudicatory documents of the people's courts shall strive to be popular, concise, and easy to understand, so that litigants can understand them; it shall strive to provide ample reasoning, thorough explanation, and appropriate application of law, so that litigants can be convinced. Good post-judgment clarification work shall be done to increase litigants' understanding and acceptance of the judgment. Attention shall be paid to the drafting and proofreading of adjudicatory documents, and errors such as writing incorrect names, writing wrong or omitting adjudicatory content, or identifying the wrong subject of responsibility shall be firmly avoided.

14. The people's courts shall establish a scientific evaluation system for judicial statistical indicators. The people's courts shall not refuse to accept a litigant's request for case filing at the end of the year for the sake of increasing the case conclusion rate. Where conditions for case filing are met, case filing shall not be delayed. If a litigant's case is refused or delayed by the people's court for this reason, the litigant may report to the higher people's court, and the higher people's court shall conduct an investigation; if the report is verified, a notice of criticism shall be issued within the jurisdiction. If a litigant is persuaded to withdraw the lawsuit, or the lawsuit or enforcement proceedings are suspended without authorization, for the sake of increasing the case conclusion rate, the litigant may report to the higher people's court, and the higher people's court shall conduct an investigation; if the report is verified, a notice of criticism shall be issued within the jurisdiction, and the relevant personnel shall be held accountable.

15. The people's courts shall actively coordinate with relevant departments to promote the establishment of a judicial assistance fund, strictly handle the reduction, exemption, and deferral of litigation costs in accordance with the law, and increase social assistance efforts for victims in various types of cases where the perpetrator is unable to compensate or the person subject to enforcement has no property available for enforcement, as well as for other litigants in difficulty involved in litigation.

16. The people's courts shall establish a case supervision card system. Upon conclusion of a case, litigants voluntarily fill in their evaluation of the work of the case-handling personnel. The litigants' evaluation of the litigation activities of the case-handling personnel shall be included in the scope of assessment of trial and enforcement work.

17. The people's courts shall designate specialized institutions and personnel responsible for complaint letter and visit affairs, earnestly perform daily complaint letter and visit work; further improve the system for presidents and division chiefs to receive visitors, regularly receiving visiting members of the public; further strengthen the supervision system for complaint letters and visits, implement complaint letter and visit responsibilities, earnestly address repeated complaints letters and visits, and promptly provide feedback on the handling results to the individuals who sent the letters or made the visits.
